title: [Bug]: Vitest/Vite config file fails to load on Windows with "[UNRESOLVED_ENTRY] Cannot resolve entry module", despite the file provably existing at the exact reported path
body:
### Reproduction link or steps

A live REPL/StackBlitz reproduction isn't possible for this one, since it's
specific to a nested Windows working directory structure created by Gitea's
act_runner (v3.3.1) running CI jobs directly on the host (no Docker).
Manual reproduction:

1. On Windows (reproduced on Server 2019, build 10.0.17763), create a
   nested working directory a few levels deep from a drive root, e.g.:
   C:\act-work\<anything>\hostexecutor\

2. Inside it, npm install vite@8.2.0 vitest@4.1.11 (rolldown 1.2.1 is
   bundled by vite automatically).

3. Add vitest.config.mjs:
   import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
   export default defineConfig({ test: { include: ['tests/**/*.test.mjs'] } })

4. Run: npx vitest run

Fails every time at config-loading, before even looking for test files.
Renaming to vitest.config.ts changes nothing (same failure, same message).

### What is expected?

vitest.config.mjs should load normally - the file demonstrably exists,
is readable, and Node's own fs.existsSync confirms it, at the exact path
the error later claims is unresolvable.

### What is actually happening?

failed to load config from C:\act-work\7dcc6f7954297e51\hostexecutor\vitest.config.mjs
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Startup Error ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
Error: Build failed with 1 error:
[UNRESOLVED_ENTRY] Cannot resolve entry module C:\act-work\7dcc6f7954297e51\hostexecutor\vitest.config.mjs.
    at aggregateBindingErrorsIntoJsError (.../node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/error-BgfXq0Tb.mjs:48:18)
    at #build (.../node_modules/rolldown/dist/shared/rolldown-DP_p9pd3.mjs:132:34)
    at async bundleConfigFile (.../node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:36962:17)

A diagnostic step immediately before this failure, same process, plain
Node.js APIs: process.cwd() and fs.existsSync('vitest.config.mjs') both
confirm the file is exactly where expected. Rules out a working-directory
mismatch, a stale cwd, or the file being genuinely absent.

Traced the code path: Vite's bundleConfigFile calls rolldown({ input:
fileName, ... }) with no explicit cwd, so rolldown/src/utils/bindingify-
input-options.ts:82 defaults cwd to process.cwd() (confirmed correct
above). Since there's no importer for the entry module, resolution goes
through rolldown_resolver/src/resolver.rs:167:
  selected_resolver.resolve(self.cwd.as_path(), specifier)
where `specifier` is already the full absolute path. Suspect oxc_resolver's
resolve(base_dir, specifier) isn't short-circuiting when specifier is
already absolute - oxc_resolver has had at least one prior, related
Windows path-handling fix (properly handle DOS device paths in
strip_windows_prefix, oxc_resolver 6.0.0), though that one concerned a
different mechanism (very long paths triggering extended-path syntax)
than what's happening here.

Ruled out: symlinks/junctions (confirmed via Get-Item -Force showing no
LinkType), simple deep nesting in the abstract (reproduces fine on Linux
with an equivalently deep plain directory), file extension (.ts and .mjs
fail identically), and a custom act_runner workdir_parent setting (still
fails identically with a short, non-nested parent path).

### System Info

```Shell
System:
    OS: Windows 10 10.0.17763
    CPU: (4) x64 Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU           X3363  @ 2.83GHz
    Memory: 11.27 GB / 15.99 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.18.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
    npm: 11.16.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 151.0.7922.174
    Internet Explorer: 11.0.17763.2989
```

### Any additional comments?

Encountered this while setting up a self-hosted Gitea Actions runner
(act_runner v3.3.1) running CI jobs directly on Windows, no Docker. Happy
to run additional diagnostics on the actual machine if useful - it's a
dedicated CI box, not a one-off VM, so it stays available for follow-up.
